rounds.text: Surana Solar Ltd carries severe fundamental and valuation risks that are heavily underscored by its rules-based screen score of 33 out of 100, which rates the stock a SELL with low confidence [E44]. The company exhibits abysmal profitability metrics, with a Return on Equity (ROE) of -0.2% [E8], Return on Assets (ROA) of -0.09% [E7], and Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of a negligible 0.08% [E9], heavily lagging behind sector benchmarks. This lack of earning power translates into an alarming EV/EBITDA multiple of 96.41x, which stands in stark contrast to the sector benchmark of 12.32x [E10]. Furthermore, earnings quality is suspect as they rely on other income of Rs 1.18 Cr [E42], while the business suffers from a low interest coverage ratio [E41]. Long-term wealth destruction is evident in the 10-year compounded share price growth of -1% [E12] and a 1-year plunge of -30% [E15]. Institutional confidence is actively eroding, with promoter holdings dropping significantly by 15.92 percentage points from Dec 2023 to Sep 2026 [E26] and overall institutional money flow reading negative [E29]. Technically, the stock languishes below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E32], demonstrates a weak relative-strength rating of 15 against the Nifty 500 [E33], and carries a brutal historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.0% alongside extreme annualized volatility of 72.7% [E35, E36]. Conceded: the company is almost debt free with a comfortable current ratio of 9.60x and positive free cash flow [E21, E22, E23, E40].
